items.stem: Which TWO adjustments are typically made to profit before tax when preparing operating cash flows under the indirect method? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: non-cash depreciation and amortisation are added back.

options.text: Adjusting for changes in working capital such as receivables and payables
options.rationale: Correct: working-capital movements are adjustments under the indirect method.

options.text: Adding the full cost of new property, plant and equipment purchased
options.rationale: Capital expenditure is an investing outflow, not an operating adjustment.
Share issues are financing, not operating adjustments.

items.stem: A finance manager includes the purchase of a machine acquired under a lease (no cash paid at inception) as a cash outflow in investing activities. Why is this incorrect?

options.text: It is a non-cash transaction at inception and is excluded from the statement of cash flows, with disclosure instead
options.rationale: Correct: non-cash transactions are excluded from the statement and disclosed separately.

options.text: Leased assets are always operating outflows
options.rationale: The issue is that no cash moved at inception, not the category.

options.text: All asset purchases are financing outflows
options.rationale: Asset purchases are investing, but here no cash moved.

options.text: Leases can never appear in any disclosure
options.rationale: Non-cash transactions are disclosed, just not in the cash-flow lines.
